newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-NEVIN MAKES IT BACK TO SCOTLAND.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-NEVIN MAKES IT BACK TO SCOTLAND.

text.p: Former Scotland international Pat Nevin played his first Scottish premier division match on Saturday on the opening day of the new season that kicked off without the big two Glasgow clubs.
Nevin's new employers Kilmarnock drew 0-0 at Aberdeen, Motherwell were comfortable 2-0 winners at Dunfermline and newly-promoted St Johnstone drew 1-1 with Dundee United.
Tommy Coyne scored both goals for Motherwell, his first a penalty and the second a back-heel on the volley.
Champions Rangers, setting out on a campaign to land a record 10th successive title, meet Hearts at a sold-out Ibrox on Monday while Celtic are at Hibs on Sunday.

Nevin, 32, who joined the Scottish Cup winners on Friday from Tranmere Rovers in England, went on as a second-half substitute but was unable to put the ball past his old international goalkeeper team mate Jim Leighton.

The goalless scoreline was hard on Aberdeen but might have been expected -- they have been unbeaten on the first day of the season for 11 years and had more draws than any club in the league last season.

Nevin, who had spent his career south of the border before Saturday, was pleased however. "Fourteen years later, I've managed to get back up the road," the former Chelsea and Everton winger said afterwards. "Its brilliant to be back. I've always really wanted to play at the top level in Scotland before I retired.
"It was just a shame that there were no goals."
